title: finapp — platform baseline
description: The Phase 0 operational picture: is the instance up, is the outbox draining, and is the connection pool the bottleneck. Provisioned from git (P0-TSK-029); edit the file, not the UI.

panels.title: Pending events
panels.description: Unpublished outbox events, dead-lettered ones included. Depth alone is ambiguous — a thousand published within the second is healthy — so read it beside the age panel.

panels.title: Oldest unpublished
panels.description: How long the oldest unpublished event has waited. This is what separates 'busy' from 'stuck': a growing age with a flat depth means the relay is not draining.

panels.title: Outbox backlog over time
panels.description: Depth and age together. Absent data — not zero — is what a gauge reports when the database cannot be read, so a gap here is an outage rather than an empty outbox.

panels.title: HTTP requests by outcome
panels.description: Framework metrics, not ours — useful, and not a contract. A rise in 5xx here beside a flat 4xx is our fault; the reverse is a client's.

panels.title: Connection pool
panels.description: The failure ADR-0016 and the connection-pool debt both name: ten instances at Hikari's default exhaust PostgreSQL's default max_connections before doing any work. Pending threads rising while active is flat is waiting, not load.

panels.title: Recovery initiations
panels.description: THE account-takeover signal (PHASE_1_PLAN.md §10). A campaign is a rise here — and a rise in `refused` is a probe against identifiers that do not exist, which the 202 response deliberately hides from the caller and cannot hide from this.

panels.title: Authentication outcomes and lockouts
panels.description: Failure rate is noisy and mostly benign; a spike in LOCKOUTS is credential stuffing. Two meters rather than a third tag value, so the second signal is not buried in the first's noise.

panels.title: Second-factor challenges
panels.description: Refusals rising is somebody holding a stolen password and failing at the second factor. The REASON — wrong code, replayed, no factor — lives in the audit trail and never in a tag.

panels.title: Live sessions
panels.description: max(), NEVER sum(): the gauge is read from the database, so every instance reports the same fleet-wide figure and summing ten replicas would report ten times the truth. Absent rather than zero when the database is unreadable — a comforting zero is not alertable.

panels.title: Session lifetime, when its owner ended it
panels.description: ONE POPULATION, and it is not all sessions: expiry is derived and never observed (ADR-0030), so expired sessions cannot appear here. Bulk revocation and step-up rotation are excluded too. The MEAN rather than a quantile: a Timer publishes no histogram buckets without publishPercentileHistogram(), whose cardinality this low-volume signal does not earn, and client-side percentiles do not aggregate across replicas. DashboardQueriesResolveTest caught the first version querying _bucket.

panels.title: Case throughput
panels.description: finapp.kyc.case by outcome (PHASE_2_PLAN.md §10): opened at creation, approved/rejected at decision, counted at the store seam so every door - the endpoint, the consumer, KYB registration and both decision paths - moves it. The straight-through rate is derivable as approved over opened. Per-instance counters: aggregate with sum(rate(...)).

panels.title: Check outcomes
panels.description: finapp.kyc.check as normalised by us, never a provider verdict (INV-KYC-01). A rising indeterminate is a provider degrading - which is exactly the moment this series must already exist, and why it is registered eagerly and unconditionally (P2-TSK-020).

panels.title: Review queue
panels.description: Checks awaiting a person (PHASE_2_PLAN.md §10: the queue nobody watches is the queue that ages). A fleet-wide gauge read from the database, so every instance reports the same figure: max(), NEVER sum() - summing ten replicas reports ten times the truth.

panels.title: Provider latency
panels.description: Verification provider round-trip time, refusals included - the port is total, so a timeout or a 5xx is a timed result, never an exception (ADR-0008). The MEAN, for the session-lifetime panel's reason: a Timer publishes no histogram buckets without publishPercentileHistogram(), whose cardinality this signal does not earn.

panels.title: Consent grants and withdrawals
panels.description: finapp.consent.grant and finapp.consent.withdrawal by purpose (PHASE_2_PLAN.md §10): a withdrawal spike is a trust event worth seeing, which is why it is its own meter rather than an outcome tag buried in the grant rate. The purpose tag is bounded by the closed ConsentPurpose enum (MetricNames.ALLOWED_TAG_KEYS records the decision).

panels.title: Trial balance by currency
panels.description: INV-ACC-01 as a series (P3-TSK-019): 0 verified balanced, 1 out of balance, NaN unverifiable. Zero, or an incident - alert on any non-zero value. Fleet-wide from every instance: max(), NEVER sum().

panels.title: Projection drift
panels.description: Accounts where recomputation from postings disagrees with ledger.account_balance (INV-BAL-02, P3-TSK-010) - including a holds_minor no ACTIVE hold row explains (P3-TSK-020). Zero at all times; alert on any non-zero value. Fleet-wide: max(), NEVER sum().

panels.title: Active holds
panels.description: Holds currently ACTIVE, system-wide (P3-TSK-020): hold utilisation, a count never an amount. NaN means the count could not be read - absent is alertable, a comforting zero is not. Fleet-wide: max(), NEVER sum().

panels.title: Journal-write commands by outcome
panels.description: finapp.ledger.posting (P3-TSK-020): posting, reversal and adjustment commands through the ledger's one write path. posted ran and appended; replayed returned a recorded outcome; refused threw - the failure rate an operator watches when Phase 4 makes this the hot path.

panels.title: Posting latency
panels.description: finapp.ledger.posting.latency: the duration a caller experiences on the write path, every outcome. No histogram buckets are published (the P1-TSK-029 lesson) - these are max and the rate-derived mean.

panels.title: Account lifecycle
panels.description: finapp.accounts.account (P3-TSK-020): customer accounts opened and closed. Only the acting call counts - a converged retry, a replayed key and the losers of a concurrent close are never throughput (P2-TSK-020's discipline).

panels.title: Transfer commands by outcome
panels.description: finapp.transfers.transfer (P4-TSK-011): the first customer-visible money movement, by outcome. completed and failed are acting judgements; replayed is a retried key returning its recorded judgement (INV-IDEM-01); reversed is the operator's correction; refused is a command declined with nothing written - a rise in refused is somebody probing destinations.

panels.title: Transfer latency
panels.description: finapp.transfers.transfer.latency (P4-TSK-011): duration of the transfer execution command, every outcome of POST /v1/transfers - a timer recording only successes would flatter exactly the incident an operator is trying to see. Read from _count/_sum/_max; no histogram buckets are published (the P1-TSK-029 lesson).

panels.title: Idempotency conflicts
panels.description: finapp.transfers.conflict (P4-TSK-011): INV-IDEM-03 fingerprint conflicts on the transfer command - a known key presented with a materially different request. A security signal: a stranger replaying logged keys (ADR-0004's owning-principal fingerprint refusing them). The healthy reading is a flat zero.

panels.title: Beneficiary lifecycle
panels.description: finapp.transfers.beneficiary (P4-TSK-011): saved destinations added and removed. Only the acting call counts - a converged retry is never throughput (P3-TSK-020's discipline).

panels.title: Payment judgements by outcome
panels.description: finapp.payments.attempt (P5-TSK-017): ACTING attempt judgements only - a replay, a converged retry and the losers of a racing resolution are never counted, whichever of the four resolvers applied the outcome. unknown is the honest state INV-LIFE-03 requires when a provider's answer is lost: a judgement, not a failure, settled later by a resolver.

panels.title: Provider latency by operation
panels.description: finapp.payments.provider.latency (P5-TSK-017): EVERY call to the payment provider - approvals, declines, timeouts and dropped connections alike, recorded in a finally. A rising max with a flat mean is the ambiguity window opening: the calls that time out are exactly the ones that strand payments in an unknown state.

panels.title: Refund judgements by outcome
panels.description: finapp.payments.refund (P5-TSK-017): acting refund judgements. completed released the customer's hold and posted the return; failed released with nothing posted; unknown left the funds visibly reserved until a resolver settles it.

panels.title: Payments stranded in an unknown state
panels.description: finapp.payments.unknown.active (P5-TSK-017): attempts and refunds sitting in an honestly-unknown state, system-wide. Temporary by design - the sweeper and the webhook resolver settle them - so a sustained non-zero value means neither is getting there, and a refund among them is a customer's money behind a standing hold. Fleet-wide: max(), never sum(). No data here means UNREADABLE, never healthy: the gauge publishes NaN rather than a false zero.

panels.title: Oldest unknown payment
panels.description: finapp.payments.unknown.age (P5-TSK-017): how long the OLDEST unknown operation has been unknown, measured from the state's own entry the way the sweeper measures it. The stuck-payment alert's series: a flat count while this climbs is ambiguity that is not being resolved.

panels.title: Webhook deliveries by outcome
panels.description: finapp.payments.webhook (P5-TSK-017): what became of each delivery at the door. processed applied an effect, duplicate was absorbed by the inbox (INV-IDEM-04), refused failed authentication or the evidence bound, unmappable was authentic but named no operation we minted. A rise in refused is somebody probing the door; a rise in unmappable is an integration break.

panels.title: Checkout sessions by outcome
panels.description: finapp.checkout.session (P6-TSK-008): how the platform's offers ENDED, counted once per session on the transition that committed it. completed_late is money that landed after the offer expired (INV-MER-06): if it is not rare, the offer window is too short or the provider too slow.

panels.title: Conversion age by outcome
panels.description: finapp.checkout.conversion.age (P6-TSK-013): creation to completion, once per completion. completed measures the customer inside the window; completed_late measures the provider after it - kept apart so the rare late ones cannot swallow the mean.

panels.title: Fee assessments
panels.description: finapp.merchant.fee.assessed (P6-TSK-013): merchant-bound captures that assessed the platform's fee, once per capture however many resolvers raced it. A count, never an amount (INV-AUD-02).

panels.title: Payout judgements by outcome
panels.description: finapp.merchant.payout (P6-TSK-013): acting judgements only, counted post-commit at the door that applied them. completed released the hold and posted, failed released it, unknown left the merchant's money reserved until the sweep resolves it. A payout that went unknown and then completed is two judgements.

panels.title: Payouts without an answer
panels.description: finapp.merchant.payout.unknown.active (P6-TSK-013): every UNKNOWN payout, and every DISPATCHED one past the resolution sweep's own bound - each a merchant's money behind a standing hold. Sustained non-zero means the sweep is not getting there. Fleet-wide: max(), never sum(). No data here means UNREADABLE, never healthy: the gauge publishes NaN rather than a false zero.

panels.title: Oldest unanswered payout
panels.description: finapp.merchant.payout.unknown.age (P6-TSK-013): how long the oldest of those has waited, measured the way the sweep measures it - an UNKNOWN payout from its entry into that state, an overdue dispatch from its latest send permit. The stuck-payout alert's series.

panels.title: Payout destination changes pending
panels.description: finapp.merchant.destination.pending (P6-TSK-011): proposals awaiting a second operator, and approvals still cooling off. A change nobody expected, showing up here during its cooling-off, is what this panel exists to make visible. Fleet-wide: max(), never sum().

panels.title: Rails and disputes — how money travels, and how it comes back
Rail judgements by rail and type
panels.description: finapp.payments.rail.outcome (P7-TSK-015): every acting judgement - payments, refunds, withdrawals, dispute answers - by the rail that produced it, counted once however many doors and sweeps raced for it, after its transaction committed. A rail's success rate is its successes over its decided outcomes; a rise in unknown on one rail is that rail answering ambiguously. Per instance: sum().

panels.title: Rail latency by operation
panels.description: finapp.payments.rail.latency (P7-TSK-015): every call a rail's port makes, EVERY outcome - timeouts and refused connections included - by rail and operation. A rail whose max climbs is a rail in trouble before its outcomes say so. The instant scheme is timed under its own name since P7-TSK-015 (it was published as the card PSP's).

panels.title: Routing decisions
panels.description: finapp.payments.routing.decision (P7-TSK-003): decisions by chosen rail, or rail=none with the refusal's leading rejection reason. A spike with rail=none is a rail outage or a policy gap. Per instance: sum().

panels.title: Withdrawals without an answer
panels.description: finapp.payments.withdrawal.unknown.active (P7-TSK-015): every UNKNOWN withdrawal, and every DISPATCHED one past the resolution sweep's own bound - each a customer's money behind a standing hold. Sustained non-zero means the sweep is not getting there. Fleet-wide: max(), never sum(). No data here means UNREADABLE, never healthy.

panels.title: Oldest unanswered withdrawal
panels.description: finapp.payments.withdrawal.unknown.age (P7-TSK-015): how long the oldest of those has waited, measured the way the sweep measures it. The stuck-withdrawal alert's series.

panels.title: Disputes by stage
panels.description: finapp.payments.dispute (P7-TSK-015): disputes standing at each stage now. The open stages (inquiry, charged_back, represented) are the workload; the terminal ones (won, lost, accepted, closed) are the outcomes and only grow - the win rate is won / (won + lost). The chargeback ratio per merchant is the operator report, never a tag. Fleet-wide: max().

panels.title: Chargebacks near their deadline
panels.description: finapp.payments.dispute.deadline.near (P7-TSK-014): chargebacks awaiting an answer the PSP took whose network respond-by date is inside the alarm window or already missed. The alarm, never a decision. Fleet-wide: max().

panels.title: Dispute answers without a word
panels.description: finapp.payments.dispute.response.unknown.active (P7-TSK-015, INV-LIFE-03): every UNKNOWN dispute answer, and every DISPATCHED one past the resolution sweep's bound - an answer the network's deadline may overtake. Fleet-wide: max().

panels.title: Oldest unanswered dispute answer
panels.description: finapp.payments.dispute.response.unknown.age (P7-TSK-015): how long the oldest of those has waited, measured the way the sweep measures it.

panels.title: Counterparties below zero
panels.description: finapp.ledger.negative.positions (P7-TSK-013): accounts a chargeback drove below zero, by purpose - merchant debt and customer receivables. A count, never an amount. Fleet-wide: max().

panels.title: Settlement and reconciliation — what the counterparties said, and whether it matched
Proofs that must read 0
panels.description: The four must-be-0 verdicts (P8-TSK-024, PHASE_8_PLAN section 15): finapp.reconciliation.position.proof (currencies failing INV-REC-06, by purpose), finapp.reconciliation.line.unattributed (unknown lines on reconciled positions, by purpose), finapp.reconciliation.cash.proof (INV-SET-06, by currency) and finapp.reconciliation.suspense.unowned (INV-REC-09). Each tile is the worst purpose or currency; the alert names which. Counts and verdicts, never an amount - the amounts are the positions and suspense reports'. Fleet-wide: max(). No data means UNREADABLE, never healthy.

panels.title: Settlement files pending, and the oldest
panels.description: finapp.settlement.file.pending and finapp.settlement.file.age (P8-TSK-003): non-terminal files by source - those awaiting a second person's attestation included - and how long the oldest has waited (right axis). A growing age with a flat count is a file nobody is attesting or a parse that is not finishing. Fleet-wide: max().

panels.title: Source silence
panels.description: finapp.settlement.source.silence (P8-TSK-021): seconds since each source's last ACCEPTED batch, by any channel - a file that never came shows here before its expectations age into breaks. The silent-source alert's series. A source that has never been accepted reads NaN, never zero. Fleet-wide: max().

panels.title: Reconciliation runs pending, blocked, and the oldest
panels.description: finapp.reconciliation.run.pending, .run.blocked and .run.age (P8-TSK-011): incomplete runs by source, blocked ones (MUST read 0 - each is a batch nobody is matching, alerted; requeued at POST /v1/operator/reconciliation/runs/{id}/requeue) and the oldest incomplete run's age (right axis). Fleet-wide: max().

panels.title: Item dispositions and late matches
panels.description: finapp.reconciliation.item (P8-TSK-024): every settlement line's committed disposition - matched, unmatched, parked, checked, offset, errored - counted once after its chunk committed; the match rate is matched over the total. finapp.reconciliation.rematch: late records found for lines that waited, REPROCESS allocations included. Per instance: sum().

panels.title: Expectations open and overdue
panels.description: finapp.reconciliation.expectation.open, .expectation.overdue and .expectation.overdue.age (P8-TSK-007, -013): what the platform expects a counterparty to report, by source; those past their window (INV-SET-02, alerted); and the oldest overdue one's age (right axis). Fleet-wide: max().

panels.title: Open breaks by severity
panels.description: finapp.reconciliation.break.open (P8-TSK-024): the break backlog. The gauge is tagged by break type and severity; each series is collapsed fleet-wide with max() first, then the types are summed within a severity - summing instances would multiply the backlog by the instance count. The list is GET /v1/operator/reconciliation/breaks.

panels.title: Oldest open break by severity
panels.description: finapp.reconciliation.break.age (P8-TSK-024): how long the oldest open break of each severity has stood. The break-age alerts' series: CRITICAL above 0, HIGH above a day, MEDIUM above five days, LOW above fifteen. Fleet-wide: max().

panels.title: Suspense open, and the oldest
panels.description: finapp.reconciliation.suspense.open and .suspense.age (P8-TSK-010, INV-REC-05): suspense items still holding a remainder, and the oldest one's age (right axis) - suspense is never a permanent resting place. A count and an age, never an amount: the balance, CREDIT and DEBIT gross, is the audited suspense report's. Fleet-wide: max().

panels.title: Resolutions and replays
panels.description: finapp.reconciliation.resolution (P8-TSK-024): resolutions by kind and outcome - approved, rejected, withdrawn, evidenced, stale - REPUDIATE_BATCH included. finapp.reconciliation.replay (P8-TSK-022): decision replays by verdict; any diverged is a stored decision that no longer follows from its own snapshot, and raises a CRITICAL break. Per instance: sum().

panels.title: FX and cross-border — quotes, covers, proofs, payments, returns
FX quotes by outcome
panels.description: finapp.fx.quote (P9-TSK-008): quote requests per pair by outcome - issued, or refused for rate trouble or the cap. Per instance: sum(). A count, never a rate.

panels.title: Quotes closed and live
panels.description: finapp.fx.quote.closed by outcome (accepted, expired, cancelled, abandoned) and finapp.fx.quote.open, the live quotes. Fleet-wide gauge: max().

panels.title: Reference age and fetches
panels.description: finapp.fx.rate.age (seconds since the latest reference snapshot, worst pair) and finapp.fx.rate.fetch by outcome. Stale past the policy's maximum age fails quoting closed.

panels.title: Provider quote latency
panels.description: finapp.fx.provider.quote.latency by provider and outcome: the firm quote's wall time - failover health.

panels.title: Conversions executed and reversed
panels.description: finapp.fx.trade by outcome (executed, reversed) and finapp.fx.residual by direction - the residual's frequency; its amount is the revenue report's.

panels.title: Cover outcomes
panels.description: finapp.fx.cover by provider, type and outcome: executed, off plan, rejected, unknown, requoted, voided.

panels.title: Covers unanswered and open
panels.description: finapp.fx.cover.unknown.age and finapp.fx.cover.open.age by provider: the oldest unanswered execution and the oldest uncovered leg. Fleet-wide: max(). Alerts past five minutes.

panels.title: FX proofs that must read 0
panels.description: finapp.fx.proof by purpose (currencies failing the FX books proof) and finapp.fx.plan.verdict (1 clean, 0 diverged). Verdicts, never amounts.

panels.title: Outbound credits unanswered and undecided
panels.description: finapp.payments.outbound.unknown.age and finapp.payments.outbound.received.age: the oldest credit with no answer, and the oldest the provider holds undecided. Fleet-wide: max().

panels.title: Cross-border payments by corridor
panels.description: finapp.crossborder.payment by outcome - submitted, in transit, delivered, failed, cancelled, returned - and finapp.crossborder.payment.in.transit.age, the oldest undelivered payment. Counts and ages, never amounts.

panels.title: Returns and cancellations
panels.description: finapp.crossborder.return by outcome (applied, deferred, not applicable, resolved) and finapp.crossborder.cancellation by outcome (recalled, too late) - the free-option watch.

panels.title: Counterparty screening and review
panels.description: finapp.kyc.counterparty.screening by outcome, and the review backlog's age - a beneficiary held unpayable until a reviewer decides.
